summary: Consumer termination lifecycle, access + inventory: shutdown-time drain and startup-window detection
description:
Deferred from TKT-98 ai-review pass 2 (finding R3, [high] as reported, triaged incidental). PRE-EXISTING and unchanged by TKT-98 -- verified against origin/main.

On SIGTERM, `awaitShutdown` (services/access/cmd/access/main.go) drains `consumerErr` for errors that have ALREADY arrived, then shuts the HTTP server down and returns. On the common path both consumer goroutines are still unwinding at that instant, so the channel is empty, the drain finds nothing, and any genuine consumer failure that materialises during teardown (durable deleted, subscription terminated, a NATS fault) is published to a channel nobody is reading any more. The process exits 0 while a consumer really did break.

Not a TKT-98 regression. Pre-fix, `origin/main`'s select had the same empty-channel state at SIGTERM, took the `ctx.Done()` branch, and returned `srv.Shutdown`'s nil result identically. TKT-98 neither introduced nor worsened this; it only removed the coin flip on errors that HAD already arrived. The code comment at the drain states the residual explicitly.

What closing it takes (the reviewer's recommendation, and why it is its own ticket): collect one terminal result from EACH consumer within a bounded grace period after cancellation, rather than snapshotting a shared channel. That is explicit consumer-lifecycle coordination -- `awaitShutdown` would have to know how many producers exist and wait on them, and every shutdown would then carry a grace period a wedged consumer can burn.

The trade to decide at shaping time: how much should an operator-requested stop pay, in shutdown latency and in lifecycle coupling, to report a consumer failure it noticed on the way out? A defensible answer is "nothing" -- in which case this ticket closes as won't-fix WITH the reasoning recorded, which is worth more than an undocumented gap. Note the sibling constraint: whatever shape is chosen should also fit inventory (TKT-121), or the two services drift.

Test note: any fix needs a delayed-send test -- a producer that sends only AFTER awaitShutdown has entered its drain. TKT-98's tests queue values before the call and by construction cannot express this.

---

## Absorbed TKT-135 — inventory observes termination only after `startupConverge`

`services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go:503` runs `startupConverge` before `waitConsume`
at :524. `startupConverge` can run long — `reconcileAttempts = 3`, `retryBackoff = 5s`, a serial
catalog HTTP call per published pool — and a durable deleted inside that window is not noticed until
the pass ends. The residual is documented in the code comment at :515-517.

What it is and is not: **not a regression** (before TKT-127 inventory never observed `cc.Closed()` at
all), **not a false-ready lie** (`refreshStartupReadiness` stores `true` as the last statement of
`startupConverge`, so readiness is honest-false throughout). It is a **detection-latency gap** — the
process stays alive but unready, consuming nothing. Compose does not restart an unhealthy container
(ADR-017 §236-238), so process exit is the signal that matters, and it is late.

Sub-scope:
- [ ] A durable deleted while `startupConverge` runs is observed promptly, not after the pass
- [ ] The termination error stays distinguishable from a shutdown cancellation at `main`
- [ ] `refreshStartupReadiness` can never store `true` after the consume context has closed
- [ ] A `Consumer.Run`-level test (not a direct `waitConsume` call) with reconciliation blocked and
      the consume context closing — the TKT-127 tests call `waitConsume` directly and cannot catch this
- [ ] TKT-90's serialization guarantee still holds, its tests unmodified

## Why these are one ticket

Not because they are small — they are not. Because they are **one decision made once**. Both answer
"when and how does a process notice a consumer died", both meet at the same `consumerErr` channel,
and TKT-122's own text already requires that whatever shape is chosen must fit inventory too "or the
two services drift". TKT-135's stated objection — that cancelling `startupConverge` via a derived
context would make TKT-121 harder — is **gone**: TKT-121 shipped (`2fb5709`) and inventory's `main`
now filters cancellation-caused consumer errors.

Note the honest option this ticket has always carried: a defensible answer to the shutdown half is
**"an operator-requested stop should pay nothing"** — in which case that half closes as won't-fix
*with the reasoning recorded*, which is worth more than an undocumented gap. The startup half is
harder to wave away.

Test note: the shutdown half needs a **delayed-send** test — a producer that sends only *after*
`awaitShutdown` has entered its drain. TKT-98's tests queue values before the call and by
construction cannot express this.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Filed from TKT-98's SECOND ai-review pass (gpt-5.6-sol), finding R3, reported [high] and triaged **incidental** on the ground that it is pre-existing and out of TKT-98's scope -- TKT-98 is "a clean shutdown must not report a consumer error", not "a shutdown must detect consumer errors", which is a capability the service has never had.

The pre-existing claim is verified, not asserted: `git show origin/main:services/access/cmd/access/main.go` shows the same select reaching `ctx.Done()` with an empty `consumerErr` and returning `srv.Shutdown`'s nil.

Recording the disagreement honestly: the reviewer rated this **high** and said "do not ship". It shipped, with the residual documented at the call site and here. If that judgement was wrong, this ticket is where it gets corrected -- which is the point of filing it rather than only rejecting it.

Needs shaping (COS + the 8-item DoR) before Gate 1.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
### Corroborated from inventory — TKT-121's ai-review re-flagged this window, independently, at `[high]`

TKT-121 shipped inventory's `awaitShutdown` (merged `2fb5709`). Its adversarial review
(`gpt-5.6-sol`, given the diff without the plan) found this same teardown window in inventory and
returned **"Do not ship"** on it, unprompted and without having seen TKT-122 or TKT-98's R3:

> After `ctx.Done()` wins, the code checks `consumerErr` only once and immediately proceeds to
> clean shutdown if the producer has not sent yet. A single producer limits cardinality, not
> timing […] A deterministic counterexample is an empty `consumerErr` followed by an error sent
> from the shutdown callback; the current function returns nil.

It arrived at the same recommendation this ticket already records (a bounded grace wait rather than
a zero-time snapshot) and at the same test note (a delayed-send producer, which neither service's
prequeued table can express).

**What this changes for TKT-122: nothing about its scope, something about its priority.** Two
independent adversarial reviews, on two services, months apart, both rating it `[high]` on first
sight is the strongest signal available that the gap is not obvious-in-hindsight — it is what a
fresh reader concludes. The counter-argument stays exactly as this ticket already states it: the
process is stopping on operator request, and the cost of closing the window is a shutdown a wedged
consumer can delay.

**Inventory is now confirmed to have the identical window**, so this ticket's "should also fit
inventory (TKT-121), or the two services drift" is no longer forward-looking — both services are in
the state, and both `awaitShutdown` implementations would change together. Inventory's version
takes ONE non-blocking receive rather than access's drain loop (single producer, buffered-1
channel), so a bounded-wait design has to work for both cardinalities.

TKT-121 left a comment on inventory's test at the `real failure landing during shutdown` case
naming this window as uncovered and pointing here, so the boundary is visible from the test rather
than only from the board.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Gate 1 validation — re-verified against HEAD `ac2952b`

**Still real, and now a two-service concern.** `services/access/cmd/access/main.go:305` `awaitShutdown` still snapshots `consumerErr` at zero time. TKT-121 shipped the same shape in inventory and its review independently returned "do not ship" on this window — so whatever is decided here applies to both binaries. Take them together.

**Verdict: still worth doing → Ready.** Not DoR-baked: the 8-item shaping happens when the ticket is claimed, per the owner's drain-the-debt call.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
### Merged TKT-135 into this ticket (backlog drain, 2026-07-29)

Was: *access shutdown drains only already-arrived consumer errors; a failure during teardown still exits 0*

TKT-135 is now **Inventory observes durable termination only after startupConverge — a deleted durable goes unnoticed for the length of the startup pass (TKT-127 ai-review)** — absorbed above, and moved back to Backlog marked MERGED so it cannot be claimed twice. Its own thread stays readable on the board for the full filing history and review lineage.

Rationale: a plan gate + ai-review + PO gate on each half costs more than the work. See the *Why these are one ticket* section in the description.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claim — TKT-122

**Branch:** `TKT-122-consumer-termination-lifecycle` off `origin/main` @ `04e5f24`.

**Selection reason:** next in Ready by key. Zero open blockers — the only link is `absorbs TKT-135`,
parked in Backlog marked MERGED.

**Re-verified at claim time.** Both halves still open:
- Access `awaitShutdown` (`cmd/access/main.go:314-352`) drains `consumerErr` as an explicit
  **snapshot**; the code comment at :334-337 states the residual in as many words.
- Inventory runs `startupConverge` (`internal/consumer/consumer.go:503`) **before** `waitConsume`
  (:524), with the detection-latency gap documented at :515-523.

**Risk: not `risk:low`.** Shutdown and startup lifecycle in two services, with a decision that
changes what a process exit *means*.

**This ticket carries a genuine open decision, and the ticket itself says so:** a defensible answer
to the shutdown half is *"an operator-requested stop should pay nothing"*, closing that half as
**won't-fix with the reasoning recorded**. Under the Gate 2 waiver that call is mine. I will not
treat "the ticket exists therefore build something" as the answer — the ticket explicitly warns
against it, and the code comments already record the trade deliberately rather than by oversight.

**One asymmetry the plan must respect** (verified, not assumed): access has **two** consumer
goroutines sharing `consumerErr`, inventory has **one** on a buffered-1 channel. Inventory's
`main.go:234-239` documents that divergence as deliberate — *"the loop comes back if and when a
second producer does"*. Any shared shape must not silently re-couple them.

---

### ⚠️ Gate waiver — this ticket ran GATELESS (process experiment)

Same waiver as TKT-116/117/119; the repo owner waived all four human gates for this run.

| Gate | Normally | This run |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — priority | human moves Backlog → Ready | already given |
| 2 — plan approval | human approves the plan | **agent self-resolves**; prefer the critique's recommendation, else the most reversible option. Recorded in `kind=plan-final`. |
| 3 — review + merge | human reviews and squash-merges | **agent merges** after the ai-review converges; review-guide posted first as the audit record |
| 4 — PO acceptance | PO validates the COS | **agent self-validates** against test evidence on merged code |

Unchanged: `config.models` routing with no substitution, cross-model review for plan and code, TDD
with tests observed red first, `make check` green before every push and after the merge, all marker
comments, no AI attribution.

**Model routing:** `plan` = `gpt-5.6-sol` · `planReview` = `main-agent` · `implement` = `main-agent`
· `aiReview` = `gpt-5.6-sol`.

**No CI:** no Actions minutes, so `make check` is the sole gate; branch protection not enforced (403).

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Plan draft — TKT-122
**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-sol`** (codex `task --effort high`, read-only), per `config.models.plan`.
Briefed with the build/won't-fix question on half A framed as genuinely open. Verbatim below;
critique in `kind=plan-final`.

---

### Draft plan — TKT-122

**Decision** — **Half A: won’t-fix. Half B: build.**

Half A’s late shutdown error is real, but its exit status has no useful consumer during an operator-requested stop. Waiting for consumer completion would lengthen and couple shutdown for diagnostic value only. Record that trade explicitly in a new ADR and link the existing comments to it.

Half B stands independently: before shutdown, an unready-but-running Inventory container is not restarted by Compose, so delayed process exit is an actionable liveness gap.

**Half A analysis**

Access has two producers sharing a capacity-two error channel (`services/access/cmd/access/main.go:256-261`), whereas Inventory has one producer and a capacity-one channel (`services/inventory/cmd/inventory/main.go:166-167`). Their snapshot drains deliberately cannot see later sends (`services/access/cmd/access/main.go:334-337`, `services/inventory/cmd/inventory/main.go:241-244`).

What consumes the status:

- A returned error becomes exit 1 (`services/access/cmd/access/main.go:49-51`, `services/inventory/cmd/inventory/main.go:46-48`).
- Both services inherit `restart: unless-stopped`, not `on-failure` (`compose.yaml:29`, `compose.yaml:165-166`, `compose.yaml:267-268`). Unexpected process termination causes a restart regardless of whether the status was 0 or non-zero; a manual Compose stop suppresses restart.
- Health is separate: Compose probes the binaries’ `/readyz` healthcheck (`compose.yaml:54-59`), but ADR-017 states that Compose does not act on an unhealthy result (`docs/adr/ADR-017-domain-event-schema-evolution.md:236-238`).
- The broker smoke test observes a restart plus the durable-named diagnostic, not the numeric status (`smoke/access_consumer_test.go:60-68`).
- CI invokes `make check` (`.github/workflows/check.yaml:58`), whose smoke stack is deliberately torn down with `compose down` (`scripts/smoke.sh:56-57`). It does not inspect service exit status during teardown.

Therefore, once SIGTERM has already made readiness false and the process is stopping, non-zero exit buys only a historical “failure during requested shutdown” classification. It does not restore consumption, reroute traffic, trigger a different restart decision, or fail CI.

A grace period—even bounded—spends part of the platform’s shutdown budget waiting on the component most likely to be wedged. Access has the higher cost because it must collect two terminal results and one slow consumer holds the process open; Inventory would wait for only one, but the exit-status benefit remains equally absent. Moving the snapshot after HTTP shutdown merely relocates the window; an unbounded join can hang; a bounded join adds latency without closing the guarantee beyond its timeout.

Record in `docs/adr/ADR-036-consumer-termination-observation.md`:

- The snapshot semantics are intentional on operator-requested shutdown.
- No service waits for N consumer results after signal cancellation.
- Already-arrived genuine failures still win, preserving the current TKT-98/TKT-121 behavior.
- Access’s two producers versus Inventory’s one changes cost, not policy.
- Reopen only if:
  - a future orchestrator/alerting system distinguishes zero from non-zero SIGTERM exits;
  - an incident shows a teardown-only error contains unique actionable evidence unavailable from logs/metrics;
  - consumer termination obtains a documented upper bound and the deployment has a formal shutdown budget that can pay it.

Update ADR-034’s stale “open” references for TKT-121/TKT-135/TKT-122 (`docs/adr/ADR-034-shared-durable-consumer-lifecycle.md:165-175`, `docs/adr/ADR-034-shared-durable-consumer-lifecycle.md:189-192`) and cross-reference ADR-036 from both `awaitShutdown` residual comments. Do not change either function.

**Design**

Half B changes `Consumer.Run` immediately after `cons.Consume`, before `startupConverge`. Today convergence begins at `services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go:503`, while termination observation does not begin until `:524`.

The delay can include three attempts (`services/inventory/internal/consumer/reconcile.go:32`), two 5-second backoffs (`services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go:61`, `services/inventory/internal/consumer/reconcile.go:113`), and a serial catalog HTTP request for every published pool (`services/inventory/internal/consumer/reconcile.go:43-44`). Those requests already carry the supplied context (`services/inventory/internal/consumer/catalog.go:280-286`).

Implement this lifecycle in `Consumer.Run`:

1. Create a derived startup context and a buffered one-result channel.
2. Start exactly one goroutine calling the existing package-local `waitConsume(ctx, cc.Closed(), ...)` immediately after `Consume`.
3. When `waitConsume` returns, cancel the derived startup context and publish its result. For asynchronous termination, reassert the false latch under `readinessMu` so it is serialized against startup’s possible true transition.
4. Run `startupConverge` synchronously with the derived context. Context-aware catalog/store work unwinds promptly; keeping it synchronous ensures no reconciliation goroutine can outlive `Run` and later restore readiness.
5. If convergence was canceled by consumer termination, return the existing non-wrapping durable diagnostic from `waitConsume`, not `startupConverge`’s `context.Canceled`.
6. If cancellation came from the parent signal context, `waitConsume` returns nil and `Run` preserves its existing `fmt.Errorf("consumer stopped: %w", ctx.Err())` tail.
7. After ordinary convergence, consume the same result channel instead of invoking `waitConsume` a second time.

In `refreshStartupReadiness`, while still holding `readinessMu`, check `ctx.Err()` immediately before `ready.Store(true)`. This covers the case where a reconciliation dependency returns a benign result after its context was canceled. The current true store is the last readiness action (`services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go:458-473`).

TKT-90 remains intact: its guarantee is that the future-schema path commits quarantine before taking `readinessMu` and latching false (`services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go:236-247`), while startup’s quarantine check and true latch hold the same mutex (`services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go:458-472`). Thus startup cannot overwrite a committed skew latch with true. Do not modify TKT-90’s tests (`services/inventory/internal/consumer/reconcile_test.go:140`, `:152`, `:162`).

Rejected alternatives:

- A select only between retries: does not interrupt the currently blocked catalog call.
- Running convergence in a goroutine and returning immediately: permits post-`Run` writes, including a late true readiness store.
- Receiving `cc.Closed()` independently in several places: duplicates lifecycle arbitration and risks divergent diagnostics.
- Adding a new shared framework: ADR-034 explicitly leaves startup readiness gates with services (`docs/adr/ADR-034-shared-durable-consumer-lifecycle.md:141-145`). Reuse `durableconsumer.Wait`; add nothing beside it.

**Open decisions**

1. **Half A:** won’t-fix, documented in ADR-036.
2. **Does Half B stand alone?** Yes. During normal operation, unhealthy alone causes no Compose recovery; late process exit prolongs an unready, non-consuming process.
3. **Race shape:** one asynchronous `waitConsume` started immediately after `Consume`; its result cancels a derived context passed to the synchronous `startupConverge`.
4. **Error distinction:** propagate `waitConsume`’s non-wrapping diagnostic on termination. Both mains ignore an error only when their signal context is canceled and the error wraps `context.Canceled` (`services/access/cmd/access/main.go:359-360`, `services/inventory/cmd/inventory/main.go:271-272`). Inventory’s existing main test pins the handwritten termination diagnostic as a real failure (`services/inventory/cmd/inventory/shutdown_test.go:17-25`, `:61-62`).
5. **Smallest Half B change:** `Consumer.Run`, the final true-latch guard in `refreshStartupReadiness`, and one `Consumer.Run`-level test. No API, configuration, migration, or main arbitration changes.
6. **Shared package:** nothing new. `durableconsumer.Wait` already owns termination classification and diagnostic production (`shared/go/durableconsumer/wait.go:77-83`); the startup gate remains Inventory policy.

**Test seam**

- **Half A:** no executable test is added because the delayed-send behavior is deliberately accepted. Adding a test expecting the delayed error to win would encode the rejected bounded-join policy. If reopened, the first red test must be a delayed producer that sends only after `awaitShutdown` enters its drain; the current pre-filled tests cannot fail for this window.
- **Half B:** `Consumer.Run` with a fake JetStream → Stream → Consumer → ConsumeContext chain. A blocking resolver signals that reconciliation has started, waits for its derived context cancellation, then returns a benign result. Close the fake consume context and assert prompt cancellation, false readiness, and the durable diagnostic.

**Test plan**

1. Red-first: add `TestRunObservesTerminationDuringStartupConverge` to `services/inventory/internal/consumer/run_test.go`.
   - Current code fails by timing out because only the direct `waitConsume` tests exist (`services/inventory/internal/consumer/run_test.go:21-27`, `:51`).
   - Gate fake `ConsumeContext.Stop` so the test can inspect readiness before `Run`’s final deferred false latch hides an illicit startup `Store(true)`.
2. After implementation, assert:
   - termination cancels blocked reconciliation within the test deadline;
   - readiness never becomes true after termination observation;
   - `Run` returns the exact durable-named error;
   - the error does not wrap `context.Canceled`;
   - releasing the Stop gate lets `Run` finish without a goroutine leak.
3. Leave existing TKT-90, TKT-121, TKT-127, and shared `Wait` tests unmodified.
4. Run:
   - `go test ./internal/consumer` from `services/inventory`;
   - `go test -race ./internal/consumer`;
   - repository gate `make check`.
5. No new broker smoke test: TKT-99 already proves real NATS durable deletion closes `ConsumeContext.Closed()` (`smoke/access_consumer_test.go:54-68`); this ticket’s missing seam is Inventory’s in-process startup arbitration.

**DoD**

- [x] Plan recommends Half A won’t-fix with explicit rationale and reopening evidence.
- [ ] ADR-036 records that decision; both shutdown comments link to it.
- [ ] Durable closure cancels an in-progress startup convergence promptly.
- [ ] Termination returns the durable diagnostic; clean signal cancellation remains filterable at `main`.
- [ ] `refreshStartupReadiness` cannot leave readiness true after lifecycle cancellation.
- [ ] New test enters through `Consumer.Run`, with reconciliation blocked and `cc.Closed()` closing.
- [ ] TKT-90’s quarantine/readiness serialization and tests remain unmodified.
- [ ] ADR-034’s stale TKT-121/TKT-135/TKT-122 status is corrected.
- [ ] `make check` passes.

**Files**

- `docs/adr/ADR-036-consumer-termination-observation.md` — new decision record for both halves.
- `docs/adr/ADR-034-shared-durable-consumer-lifecycle.md` — resolution/status references.
- `services/access/cmd/access/main.go` — comment-only ADR link; no shutdown behavior change.
- `services/inventory/cmd/inventory/main.go` — comment-only ADR link; no shutdown behavior change.
- `services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go` — early termination observer, derived context, serialized false latch, guarded true latch.
- `services/inventory/internal/consumer/run_test.go` — new `Consumer.Run`-level red-first test and local fakes.

No changes to `shared/go/durableconsumer/`, `smoke/`, Compose, APIs, or generated code.

**Risks / Cons**

- Adds one lifetime goroutine to Inventory’s consumer; the result channel must be buffered and every path must cancel or stop the consume context so it cannot leak.
- Prompt exit still relies on reconciliation dependencies honoring context. The catalog request does; its production client is additionally bounded to five seconds (`services/inventory/cmd/inventory/main.go:164`).
- Serializing termination with `readinessMu` adds lifecycle responsibility to an existing TKT-90 mutex; comments and the adversarial test must make that third writer explicit.
- The exact simultaneous SIGTERM/consumer-closure ambiguity remains the shared `Wait` contract; this plan does not redefine it.
- Half A continues to permit exit 0 when a genuine consumer failure materializes only after the shutdown snapshot. That is the accepted cost, not a claim that the gap disappeared.

**Migrations / schema**

None. Startup convergence changes only runtime cancellation ordering; ADR-022’s out-of-band migration placement remains untouched (`docs/adr/ADR-022-out-of-band-service-migrations.md:101-105`).

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan-final -->
### Plan-final — TKT-122 (delta on the `kind=plan` draft)

**Critique by `main-agent`** (`config.models.planReview`; drafter `gpt-5.6-sol`). **The `kind=plan`
draft as amended below is the plan.** Gate 2 waived; decisions resolved by me.

---

#### Seam verification (`git grep -n` at `04e5f24`)
Verified and correct: the two-producer/cap-2 channel (`access/main.go:256-261`) vs one-producer/cap-1
(`inventory/main.go:166-167`) · both snapshot comments (`access:334-337`, `inventory:241-244`) ·
`startupConverge` at `:503` before `waitConsume` at `:524` · `reconcileAttempts = 3`
(`reconcile.go:32`) · `retryBackoff = 5 * time.Second` (`consumer.go:61`) ·
`refreshStartupReadiness` holding `readinessMu` with `ready.Store(true)` as its **last** statement
(`consumer.go:458-473`) · TKT-90's skew latch under the same mutex (`consumer.go:245-247`) ·
`durableconsumer.Wait`'s contract (`wait.go:77-83`).

**The claim half B's whole framing rests on — "honest-false readiness, not a lie" — is TRUE.**
Checked directly rather than accepted: `refreshStartupReadiness` takes `readinessMu`, checks pending
quarantine, and `ready.Store(true)` is the final statement. So the window is detection latency, not
a false ready.

---

#### Decisions

**D1 — REJECT the new `ADR-036`. Amend `ADR-034` instead.** *(amends the draft's Half A recording)*
The draft proposes a new ADR for the won't-fix decision. ADR-034 already **owns this exact
subject** — its package doc says it covers *"how a consumer distinguishes a clean shutdown from
asynchronous termination, and what it owes the operator"* — and it already contains:
- a detailed §Consequences paragraph on **half B's** startup hole (`ADR-034:167-177`), written when
  it was deferred as TKT-135;
- a "**Still open, deliberately**" list naming **TKT-122** (access's drain snapshot) and **TKT-135**
  (`:189-192`).

Both decisions are updates to entries that already exist. A second ADR would fragment one subject
across two documents and leave ADR-034's own paragraphs stale — which the draft separately admits by
scheduling edits to them anyway. One amended ADR, not a new one plus a patched old one.
*More reversible, smaller diff, and it keeps the decision where a reader of ADR-034 looks.*

**D2 — ACCEPT half A won't-fix.** The draft's evidence chain is right and I verified the load-bearing
link independently: every Go service inherits **`restart: unless-stopped`** (`compose.yaml:29` via
the `x-go-service` anchor), *not* `on-failure`. On the operator-stop path — which is the only path
that reaches this window, since the drain runs after `ctx.Done()` — Docker suppresses restart
**regardless of exit code**. The exit status of a SIGTERM'd process changes nothing: not restart, not
routing, not CI (`scripts/smoke.sh` tears the stack down with `compose down` and never inspects
status), not the smoke assertion (which observes a restart plus the durable-named diagnostic, not a
number).

Add to the recorded reasoning: the window is also **narrower than it reads**. `Wait`'s own contract
(`wait.go:66-72`) says the `ctx.Done()` arm *"reliably wins the ordinary path"*; half A needs the
durable to die in the same instant as SIGTERM.

**D3 — AMEND: take the free half of the benefit. Log the late error at the producer.**
This is the amendment I most want the ai-review to attack, so it is stated plainly.

The draft's won't-fix reasoning is *"non-zero exit buys only a historical 'failure during requested
shutdown' classification"*. True — and that classification is worth having; what makes it not worth
having **is the price** (blocked shutdown, lifecycle coupling, a wedged consumer delaying every
stop). But there is a version with **no price at all**, which neither the ticket nor the draft
considered:

Today a late error is lost **completely** — I checked what `main` does with an error
(`access/main.go:49-51`, `inventory/main.go:46-48`): it prints to **stderr** and exits 1. So on the
normal path the operator sees the text. In half A's window there is **no stderr line and no exit
code**: the value goes to a channel nobody reads and is garbage-collected.

So: log it in the producing goroutine, before the send.

```go
go func() {
    err := cons.Run(ctx)
    if err != nil && !isShutdownConsumerError(ctx, err) {
        log.ErrorContext(ctx, "consumer stopped with an error", "err", err)
    }
    consumerErr <- err
}()
```

Zero shutdown latency, zero lifecycle coupling, no grace period, no join — and the operator gets the
classification the won't-fix rejected as too expensive. It duplicates the stderr line in the ordinary
failure case, which is a trivial cost against silently losing the teardown case. Same predicate
`awaitShutdown` already uses, so a clean cancellation stays quiet.

**This does not reopen half A.** The exit code still does not change and shutdown still does not
wait. It is the difference between *"we accept losing this signal"* and *"we accept not acting on
this signal"* — and only the second is actually justified by D2's evidence.

**D4 — ACCEPT half B's design as drafted.** The shape is right: one `waitConsume` observer started
immediately after `Consume`, its result cancelling a derived context passed to a **synchronous**
`startupConverge`. Synchronous matters and the draft says why — a convergence goroutine outliving
`Run` could store `true` after termination. The `ctx.Err()` guard inside `refreshStartupReadiness`
*while still holding `readinessMu`* is the right place for sub-item 3, because that mutex is already
the serialization point TKT-90 established.
Its rejected alternatives are all correctly rejected; the sharpest is *"a select only between
retries does not interrupt the currently blocked catalog call"*.

**D5 — ACCEPT: nothing new in `shared/go/durableconsumer/`.** ADR-034 explicitly leaves startup
readiness gates with services. Adding a startup-gate abstraction for one caller would be the
speculative-generality the ADR already refused once.

---

#### Introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model
Two, both mine:
1. **D3 — logging the late consumer error.** The only *behaviour* change in half A, added against a
   draft that recommended changing nothing there. Attack this first.
2. **D1 — folding the decision into ADR-034 instead of a new ADR-036.** A subtraction; if wrong, the
   decision is recorded somewhere less discoverable than it deserves.

#### Reasoning lens — pre-mortem (applied; what it changed)
*Assume this bounced at Gate 3. Why?*
- *"You closed the ticket as won't-fix and the information is still silently lost."* → **D3**. This
  is the failure I actually expect a reviewer to raise, and the draft's plan does not answer it.
- *"You wrote a new ADR for a decision ADR-034 already had a paragraph on."* → **D1**.
- *"Your half-B goroutine leaks on the early-return paths."* → carried from the draft's own Cons;
  the test must assert `Run` returns and the observer goroutine exits.
- *"The startup fix let readiness go true after termination."* → the `ctx.Err()` guard under
  `readinessMu`, plus a test that inspects readiness **before** `Run`'s deferred `Store(false)` can
  hide an illicit `true` (the draft's gated-`Stop` fake — a good catch, keep it).

#### Test seams (final)

| Half | Seam | Test | The input shape that lets it fail |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (D3 only) | none | — | Logging is 3 lines and a predicate already tested via `awaitShutdown`. A test asserting "a log line exists" pins a string, not behaviour. **Stated, not skipped.** |
| B | `services/inventory/internal/consumer/run_test.go` — **`Consumer.Run`-level**, not a `waitConsume` call | `TestRunObservesTerminationDuringStartupConverge` | A fake JS→Stream→Consumer→ConsumeContext chain with a **blocking resolver** that signals reconciliation has started, then waits for its derived context to cancel. Close the fake consume context mid-pass. Today this **times out** — the observer does not exist. Assert: prompt cancellation, `Run` returns the **exact durable diagnostic**, the error does **not** wrap `context.Canceled`, readiness never true (checked behind a **gated `Stop`** so the deferred false latch cannot mask an illicit true), and the observer goroutine exits. |

TKT-127's tests call `waitConsume` directly and **by construction cannot catch this** — the ticket
says so and it is verified. TKT-90's tests stay unmodified.

#### DoD → the ticket's sub-items
- [ ] Half A recorded as won't-fix **in ADR-034**, with the reopening conditions and the
      `restart: unless-stopped` evidence; both `awaitShutdown` comments point at it.
- [ ] A late consumer error is **logged** (D3) — no latency, no coupling, no exit-code change.
- [ ] A durable deleted during `startupConverge` is observed promptly.
- [ ] The termination error stays distinguishable from shutdown cancellation at `main`.
- [ ] `refreshStartupReadiness` cannot store `true` after the consume context closed.
- [ ] A `Consumer.Run`-level test with reconciliation blocked and the consume context closing.
- [ ] TKT-90's serialization holds, its tests unmodified.
- [ ] `make check` green (with `-race` on the consumer package).
